analysis.title: GS Novak - GS U.S. Industrials & Materials | China | prime | early EPS previews 19 Oct 2026
key_insights: S&P futures up 50bps pre-market, led by a technology rally after last week's 500bps sell-off. Geopolitical escalation across Ukraine/Russia and parts of France met low expectations around broader markets.

Overnight: KOSPI +176bps, Japan -62bps, Europe heavy with France -130bps. European gas approaching $90, Brent $108, WTI $101, 10-year at 5.08%, DXY $102, Bitcoin up 250bps to $82.9k, VIX down 7% pre-market.

Early industrials earnings (AYI, FUL, RPM, FAST, DAL, JBHT reported): September topline soft with a lower exit rate than the start of the quarter, and inflation is problematic across oil, freight and medical costs.
Names are not moving on results: the biggest move so far is 3%, which the desk attributes to very low gross exposure.
SLGN headlines point to a potential $3.4bn deal for Trivium Packaging. CCK reports post-market 10/19.

China September trade: exports +36.3% yoy and imports +31.0% yoy in nominal USD, both above consensus. Semiconductor exports +136% yoy and imports +75% yoy, driven almost entirely by higher prices. Trade surplus a record $133.5bn.

China September PPI +5.0% yoy vs Bloomberg consensus 4.4%, while CPI was +0.9% yoy vs 1.0% expected. The divergence shows difficulty passing upstream prices to consumers, evidence of weak domestic demand. GS raised 2026/27 PPI forecasts to 2.8%/0.3% (from 2.0%/0.0%) and cut CPI forecasts to 0.8%/0.6% (from 1.0%/1.0%).

Prime book: US equities net sold on the week (-0.9 SDs 1-year). Single stocks saw the largest net selling in 8 weeks (-1.2 SDs), with long-and-short sales at 1.5 to 1. 8 of 11 sectors net sold, led by Info Tech, Consumer Disc, Industrials and Financials. Health Care, Comm Svcs and Staples were net bought, an incrementally defensive posture.

Macro products (index and ETF) marginally net sold (-0.1 SDs), driven by risk unwinds. US-listed ETF shorts decreased 1.9%, with covering in Small Cap and Credit ETFs partly offset by shorting in Financials and Large Cap Equity ETFs.

GE reports 10/20 pre-market with a 5% implied move. The stock is down three quarters in a row and four of the last five. EV/EBITDA has fallen from 35x to 28x and P/E from 45x to 36x. Sentiment is cautious, with the conflict now six months old. Upside could come from higher 2028 guidance, growth durability commentary and an order reacceleration after a Q3 slowdown.

GM reports 10/20 with a 5% implied move and has risen four quarters in a row. It has not missed headline earnings since Q2 2022 or EBIT since Q4 2023. It is one of the few well-owned auto names, held for market share, geographic positioning and capital returns.

MMM reports 10/20 with a 5% implied move. Focus is organic growth, with expectations near 4%, and management has said organic would slow in the back half. The stock has given up all its earnings gains. Valuation is 17x EPS and 12x EV/EBITDA, in line with pre-COVID averages but cheap versus multi-industrial peers. The desk sees positioning skewing net negative.

NOC reports 10/20 with a 5% implied move. The stock is down two quarters in a row. Sentiment is negative on free cash flow fears and the recent FAXX contract loss. Shares short are at highs and nearly 2x a year ago, but low versus float and liquidity. Valuation is 17x earnings and 13x EV/EBITDA.

RTX reports 10/20 with a 4% implied move. The stock rose 7% on Q2 and is split 50/50 on earnings reactions. Short interest is low at 13.6mm shares. Focus is organic growth, Pratt margins, AOG trajectory and the munition framework agreement update.

CSX reports 10/21 after the close with a 4% implied move and has risen six quarters in a row. Short interest is a record 43mm shares (from 25mm a year ago), about 2% of float and 4 days to cover. Deal odds for UNP/NSC have come in, and investors debate whether CSX carries an M&A premium. Valuation is at the high end of its range.

PKG reports 10/21 post-market with a 4% implied move. Containerboard is one of the few crowded areas in paper and packaging, with PKG at the top, then SW and IP, on industry supply rationalization lifting prices. Valuation is 17x earnings and 10x EV/EBITDA. Shares short are at lows. The stock is range-bound $210-250, holding the 200-day, and a breakout above $240 is possible on a better update.

TSLA reports 10/21 post-market with a 6% implied move. The stock is down three quarters in a row and four of the last five, but has outperformed on better Q3 delivery data. The desk expects non-GAAP gross margins roughly flat. Essentially all top shareholders added last quarter, and short interest is range-bound at low levels.

URI reports 10/21 post-market with a 7% implied move after rising 10% (Q1) and 23% (Q2). It has become the most crowded long in machinery by elimination. Short interest fell 1.4mm shares to 2.6 days to cover, 2% of float. Watch end-market commentary, rental rates and redistribution costs.

WCN reports 10/21 post-market with no options implied move. Focus is landfill issues: the Chiquita landfill remediation under California's AB 28 and a possible elevated-temperature event at the Avena landfill. Short interest is 4mm shares, the highest in a decade, and valuation is depressed versus history.
